section_summary: This section covers the aftermath of the May 15, 1932 assassination of Japanese Premier Tsuyoshi Inukai, including German press commentary, mourning observances in Seoul, and the lifting of Japanese censorship regarding the official investigation. The bulk of the section focuses on Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's diplomatic memoirs ('Gaiko Yoroku'), encompassing press serializations and editorials in The Japan Advertiser, a 14-page English translation of its table of contents prepared by Consul William R. Langdon, and State Department correspondence regarding a potential complete English translation. The section concludes with cross-references and the subject jacket for Japanese industrialist Masao Shibusawa.

subfiles.about: Continuation of an American diplomatic despatch reporting German newspaper reactions to the assassination of Premier Inukai and growing militarism in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The despatch transmits and analyzes commentary from various German newspapers regarding the May 15 assassination of Premier Tsuyoshi Inukai. German commentators viewed the assassination as a triumph of military fascists over parliamentary government that threatened peace with Russia and China. Ambassador Sackett concludes the transmittal of these press opinions from Berlin.
subfiles.title: German Press Comment on the Assassination of Premier Inukai

subfiles.about: Report on official condolences and local memorial observances in Seoul following the assassination of Premier Inukai.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Davis reports offering condolences to Governor-General Ugaki on behalf of American residents in Korea following Premier Inukai's assassination. Inquiries revealed that the Government General would not participate in official mourning or half-mast flags. An enclosure from The Seoul Press describes a private memorial service organized by the Prefect of Seoul and attended by Japanese military officers.
subfiles.title: Observances of Mourning at Seoul for Premier Inukai

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting the lifting of Japanese censorship concerning the May 15, 1932 assassination report.
subfiles.summary: This document file note cross-references Despatch No. 412 from Tokyo regarding the lifting of the press ban on May 17, 1933. The lifting allowed the release of the Japanese government's findings on the assassination of Premier Inukai. The original document is filed under decimal file 894.00 P.R./63.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Censorship Lifted on May 15 Affair Findings

subfiles.about: Despatch excerpt discussing the publication of the Japanese government's findings on Premier Inukai's assassination.
subfiles.summary: This excerpt from Despatch No. 412 describes the lifting of censorship on May 17, 1933, allowing publication of the report on the May 15, 1932 incident. The release had been delayed from the anniversary due to last-minute protests from the Army and Navy demanding revisions and deletions. The published report implicated lower-ranking military officers while avoiding high-ranking officials and attributing the initiative to civilians.
subfiles.title: Extract from Despatch No. 412 Regarding Findings on Inukai Assassination

subfiles.about: Departmental file jacket for records concerning Viscount Kikujiro Ishii.
subfiles.summary: This is the official State Department subject jacket for records regarding Viscount Kikujiro Ishii of Japan. It establishes decimal file number 894.44-Ishii, Viscount, beginning July 1, 1930. The jacket instructs personnel not to disarrange or remove papers from the file.
subfiles.title: Subject Jacket: Viscount Kikujiro Ishii

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memoranda recommending the purchase of Viscount Ishii's published memoirs.
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs notes the publication in Tokyo of Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's diplomatic memoirs, 'Gaiko Yoron'. The author highlights the book's sections on the Asiatic Monroe Doctrine and immigration policy. The division recommends that the American Embassy in Tokyo be instructed to purchase a copy for the Department's library at the price of 3.80 yen.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Recommending Purchase of Viscount Ishii's Memoirs

subfiles.about: Transmittal despatch enclosing newspaper reviews and editorials covering Viscount Ishii's published diplomatic memoirs.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires Neville transmits seven clippings from The Japan Advertiser reviewing and analyzing Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's memoirs ('Gaiko Yoron'). The serialized articles and editorials cover the Anglo-Japanese Alliance, the 1905 Portsmouth peace negotiations, the Ishii-Lansing Agreement, the League of Nations, and U.S. immigration policy. Special attention is given to Ishii's frank commentary on American labor politics and his negotiations with Secretary Lansing.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 194: Newspaper Clippings on Viscount Ishii's Memoirs

subfiles.about: Complete English translation of the table of contents of Viscount Kikujiro Ishii's Diplomatic Memoirs.
subfiles.summary: Consul William R. Langdon provides a comprehensive 14-page translation of the detailed table of contents of Ishii's 'Gaiko Yoroku'. Book I outlines Japan's foreign relations from early history through the Meiji era, the World War, the League of Nations, and naval limitation treaties. Book II details Ishii's personal philosophies on diplomacy, statecraft, propaganda, population, and racial questions.
subfiles.title: Translation of Table of Contents of Viscount Ishii's Diplomatic Memoirs

subfiles.about: Instruction to the Tokyo Embassy inquiring whether full translations of Viscount Ishii's memoirs are planned.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the American Ambassador in Tokyo a copy of Consul Langdon's translation of the table of contents of Ishii's memoirs. The Department inquires whether the Embassy or the Japanese publisher contemplates any complete or partial English translation of the book. The transmittal references Tokyo Despatch No. 194.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 95: Inquiries Regarding Translation of Ishii's Memoirs

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on the translation status and publication plans for Viscount Ishii's memoirs.
subfiles.summary: Replying to Instruction No. 95, Chargé d'Affaires Neville reports information obtained directly from Viscount Ishii's secretary. The secretary stated that an English translation of 'Gaiko Yoroku' was currently in preparation. However, no completion date had been set and no arrangements had yet been made for publication.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 448: Translation Status of Viscount Ishii's Memoirs

subfiles.about: Departmental memoranda summarizing the available information regarding translations of Viscount Ishii's memoirs.
subfiles.summary: Following an inquiry from the Division of Eastern European Affairs, the Division of Far Eastern Affairs summarizes the status of translations of Ishii's memoirs. The memorandum confirms that the book had only been published in Japanese and that the State Department possessed only a translated table of contents. It reiterates the Tokyo Embassy's report that a private translation was underway without definite publication plans.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Translation Status of Viscount Ishii's Memoirs

subfiles.about: Letter inquiring whether the State Department or an American scholar is preparing an English translation of Viscount Ishii's memoirs.
subfiles.summary: Professor Robert J. Kerner writes to Robert F. Kelley regarding rumors that the State Department was producing an English translation of Viscount Ishii's memoirs. Kerner explains that a Japanese scholar had asked him to collaborate on publishing an English edition. He seeks clarification on whether the Department or anyone known to it is already undertaking the project.
subfiles.title: Letter from Professor Robert J. Kerner Inquiring About Ishii Translation

subfiles.about: Letter informing Professor Kerner that the State Department is not undertaking an English translation of Viscount Ishii's memoirs.
subfiles.summary: Acting Chief Packer replies to Professor Kerner's inquiry in the absence of Mr. Kelley. He clarifies that the State Department is not translating Viscount Ishii's memoirs and knows only of the Japanese edition. He mentions the Tokyo Embassy's report of a translation in progress by Ishii's secretary, the Department's 14-page table of contents translation, and excerpts printed in The Japan Advertiser.
subfiles.title: Letter to Professor Robert J. Kerner Concerning Translation of Ishii Memoirs

subfiles.about: State Department filing slip for Professor Kerner's correspondence regarding Ishii's memoirs.
subfiles.summary: This document is a departmental filing record showing that correspondence from Professor Robert J. Kerner was formally indexed and filed. It bears the filing date of September 29, 1931, under the Division of Eastern European Affairs. The matter was recorded under decimal file 894.44-Ishii, Viscount/7.
subfiles.title: Department Filing Record: Correspondence of Professor Robert J. Kerner

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet concerning comments on the publication of a translation of Ishii's diplomatic commentaries.
subfiles.summary: This Document File Note cross-references a despatch from Consul William R. Langdon at Seoul regarding Viscount Ishii's 'Diplomatic Commentaries'. It notes comments enclosed regarding the publication of an English translation of the work. The original paper is filed under decimal file 123 L 851/257.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Publication of Translation of Ishii's Diplomatic Commentaries

subfiles.about: Departmental subject jacket for records regarding Japanese industrialist Masao Shibusawa.
subfiles.summary: This is the official State Department subject jacket opening decimal file 894.44 SHIBUSAWA, MASAO on October 13, 1936. The jacket describes Masao Shibusawa as an 'Industrialist of Japan of no little importance.' Standard instructions prohibit removing papers or defacing the jacket.
subfiles.title: Subject Jacket: Masao Shibusawa
